summary.short: UK-retained version of EU Regulation 2016/679 (UK GDPR). Sets rules for controllers and processors processing personal data in the UK or offering goods or services to, or monitoring, people in the UK, covering principles, lawful bases, consent, children's consent, special-category data and transparency. This extract covers Articles 1 to 12A only.
summary.long: This extract of the UK GDPR (part 1 of 2) covers Articles 1 to 12A, with recitals as context. It applies to processing of personal data in the context of an establishment of a controller or processor in the UK (Art. 3(1)), and to controllers or processors not established in the UK that offer goods or services to, or monitor, data subjects in the UK (Art. 3(2)). Article 5 sets principles of lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation and integrity. Article 6 permits processing only on listed lawful bases, including consent, contract, legal obligation, public task and legitimate interests; a recognised legitimate interest basis requires a condition in Annex 1, which the Secretary of State may amend by regulations. Article 7 sets consent conditions. Article 8 makes processing of a child's data for information society services lawful from age 13, and below 13 only with parental consent or authorisation; the Secretary of State may vary the age between 13 and 16. Article 9 prohibits processing of special categories of data, subject to listed exceptions; Article 10 governs criminal conviction data. Article 12 requires transparent communication and responses to data subject requests, generally within one month (Art. 12A), extendable by two further months. Enforcement, supervisory authorities, international transfers and impact assessments are not in this extract. The application date is not stated in this extract.

notes: Part 1 of 2: recitals (1)-(173), Articles 1-12A and the Section 2 heading; Articles 13 onward are in part 2. No enabling act is named in this part, so no legal_basis row is given. Several provisions appear only as dot leaders (e.g. Art. 1(3), 2(3), 4(1)(A3), 4(1)(16), 6(2), 6(4), 8(1) with F59); amendment markers (F-numbers) are not decoded. 'IP completion day' appears in Art. 2(1), 3(2A) and 4(25) but is not defined in this part. Recital (173) says Directive 2002/58/EC 'should be amended accordingly'; this is not an operative amendment in this part and is not coded. Empty target_instrument_id, lei and ticker fields mean the target is not in the registry or the identifier is not verified. This part covers Articles 13 to 99 and Annexes 1 and 2. Several provisions show only headings or omitted-text markers (e.g. Art. 22, Art. 94(1), Art. 99), so their operative content is absent here. The text uses 'Commission' for the supervisory body throughout, while the Art. 77 heading reads 'Commissioner'; both are recorded as written. Art. 83(4) to (6) state fine amounts in pounds sterling as written; enforcement is not annotated in this part. Unknown target instrument IDs are recorded as empty strings because the schema requires strings.

‘personal data’ means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person
‘processing’ means any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data
‘profiling’ means any form of automated processing of personal data consisting of the use of personal data to evaluate certain personal aspects relating to a natural person
‘pseudonymisation’ means the processing of personal data in such a manner that the personal data can no longer be attributed to a specific data subject without the use of additional information
‘filing system’ means any structured set of personal data which are accessible according to specific criteria
‘controller’ means the natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data
‘processor’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which processes personal data on behalf of the controller
‘recipient’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or another body, to which the personal data are disclosed, whether a third party or not
‘consent’ of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data subject's wishes
‘personal data breach’ means a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data
‘genetic data’ means personal data relating to the inherited or acquired genetic characteristics of a natural person
‘biometric data’ means personal data resulting from specific technical processing relating to the physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics of a natural person
‘data concerning health’ means personal data related to the physical or mental health of a natural person
“direct marketing” means the communication (by whatever means) of advertising or marketing material which is directed to particular individuals
‘representative’ means a natural or legal person established in

‘group of undertakings’ means a controlling undertaking and its controlled undertakings
‘binding corporate rules’ means personal data protection policies which are adhered to by a controller or processor established
‘international organisation’ means an organisation and its subordinate bodies governed by public international law
‘third country’ means a country or territory outside the United Kingdom
